activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Line

feedback.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(1,0,0)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨1,1,1⟩.$ Find all the possible points $R$ on that line such that $RP=3\sqrt{3}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨1,0,0⟩+t⟨1,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $R$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OR} & =⟨1,0,0⟩+t⟨1,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PR} & =\overset{\to }{OR}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨1,0,0⟩+t⟨1,1,1⟩)-⟨1,0,0⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨1,1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨t,\,t,\,t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PR=3\sqrt{3},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}RP & =3\sqrt{3} \\ |\overset{\to }{PR}| & =3\sqrt{3} \\ |⟨t,\,t,\,t⟩| & =3\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}} & =3\sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt{3{t}^{2}} & =3\sqrt{3} \\ \pm t\sqrt{3} & =3\sqrt{3} \\ t & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 3$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{R}_{1}}=⟨1,0,0⟩+3⟨1,1,1⟩=⟨4,3,3⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{R}_{2}}=⟨1,0,0⟩-3⟨1,1,1⟩=⟨-2,-3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${R}_{1}(4,3,3)$ and ${R}_{2}(-2,-3,-3).$
